frozen_at: 2026-09-26 before any tick data was downloaded or inspected
hypothesis: The scheduled US 08:30 New York release window (15:30 XM server time, EET) produces a range expansion that a two-sided stop straddle can monetise after real bid/ask costs.

event.definition: The M5 bar that opens at 15:25 server time and closes at 15:30 (the Phase 13 event H21 NY open, bar index at minute 25 of hour 15).
event.reference_price: The bid close of that M5 bar = the last bid quote at or before 15:30:00.000 server time (Phase 13 code: c[i]).
event.atr: ATR(14), Wilder RMA of true range, on M5 bars built from the same feed, evaluated on the 15:25 bar (Phase 13 code: atr[i]). For the tick study M5 bars are built from ticks (bid mid-quotes) so the study is self-contained.
event.primary_days: Thursday and Friday (server date). Secondary: Monday to Wednesday, reported separately. Calendar identity: unavailable, marked as such; weekday is not converted into an event name.
event.out_of_sample: 2026-01-01 to 2026-09-25, read-only until the final table
event.validation: none separate (per the brief); the trigger, target and holding-period plateaus are read on 2025 only

orders.placed_at: 15:30:00.000 server time (first tick at or after), both orders simultaneously
orders.buy_stop: reference + 0.25 x ATR; triggers on the first tick with ASK >= level; fill = that ask (Scenario A)
orders.sell_stop: reference - 0.25 x ATR; triggers on the first tick with BID <= level; fill = that bid (Scenario A)
orders.oco: the untriggered order is cancelled with latency L after the first fill; L = 0 ms (ideal), 250 ms (realistic), 1000 ms (adverse). If the other side triggers before cancellation, both executions are modelled (Case D), never ignored.
orders.target: 0.75 x ATR from the fill price; exit on the first tick with BID >= target (long) or ASK <= target (short); fill at that quote
orders.stop: the opposite trigger level; exit on the first tick with BID <= sell level (long) or ASK >= buy level (short); fill at that quote
orders.horizon: 250 minutes from 15:30 (the Phase 13 straddle used H=250 M1 bars); an untriggered straddle at the horizon = NO TRADE; an open position at the horizon = TIMEOUT, closed at the quote
orders.note_vs_phase13_bars: The bar code filled the buy leg at trigger + spread and charged the short leg's stop an extra spread; both were more conservative than the definitions above, which follow the brief's section 2.

costs.scenario_A: observed executable quote at the triggering tick
costs.scenario_B: fill at the worse of the triggering tick and the next tick after 250 ms (a realistic acceptance delay)
costs.scenario_C: fill at the worst quote within 1000 ms after the trigger
costs.xm_overlay: Scenario B plus (XM median spread 51 pts minus the Dukascopy spread at that moment) per round trip, because the user trades an XM Standard account
costs.slippage_beyond_quotes: not observable; Scenarios B and C are the only slippage model, stated as such

classification: AMBIGUOUS_EXECUTION (both triggers on ticks with identical timestamps)
analyses_frozen: DEV-only plateaus: trigger 0.15-0.40, target 0.50-1.50, horizon 30-300 min
controls: random same-day timestamps, all weekdays, Thu/Fri random timestamps
gross vs net and cost share
acceptance: positive net expectancy under Scenario B, PF > 1, adequate count, no single event / day / week / outlier responsible, positive across the trigger and target plateaus and holding periods on 2025, positive untouched 2026, then a four-week XM demo for fills
